subtitulo: It's 2026. You have a planet, a handful of ideas that already work, and no money at all. Let's see if you can cool it down.
semilla_ayuda: Two different seeds, two different worlds.
toca_celda: Tap a tile on the planet to see what can be done there.
nada_aqui: Nothing can be built on this tile yet.
politicas_ayuda: Big policies are paid with Hope.
adopcion: The world has adopted {p}% of it
potencial: Project Drawdown: {a} to {b} Gt a year
err_bioma: That solution doesn't fit this biome.
revelada: Exposed: {nombre}. Its real effect was far smaller, and it costs the planet Life.
inf_permafrost: Tipping point: permafrost has started thawing. It releases emissions you can't switch off.
inf_corales: Tipping point: tropical coral reefs are bleaching. Life drops.
inf_amazonia: Tipping point: the Amazon is turning into savanna. More emissions.
choque: Termination shock: removing the aerosols brought the hidden heat back at once.
era2: New solutions unlocked: restoration, utility-scale solar, offshore wind and more.
dato: Real fact · {nombre}: according to Project Drawdown, it could avoid or remove {a}–{b} GtCO₂e per year.
dato_sin: Real fact · {nombre}: Project Drawdown hasn't published its potential yet; in the game it's an assumption.
fin_victoria_txt: Temperature peaked and fell for ten years in a row, with net-negative emissions.
fin_derrota_vida_txt: Without biodiversity, the planet stopped holding itself together.
fin_derrota_esperanza_txt: Without people who believe, there is no transition.
fin_derrota_tiempo_txt: 2150 arrived and the climate wasn't reversed.
pol_cerrar_carbon_txt: −15% energy emissions. Fossil lock-in makes it pricier.
pol_fin_subsidios_txt: The fossil economy starts shrinking on its own every year.
pol_moratoria_deforestacion_txt: −40% forest emissions; Life degrades much less.
ayuda_txt: Each turn is a year. Tap a tile, build a Project Drawdown solution and upgrade it. Solutions cost ⚡ and ⛏, which refill every year up to a cap: what you don't spend is lost. Look after Life and Hope: if either hits 0, you lose. Beware of traps: they're cheap and seem to work… until they're exposed. You win when temperature falls ten years in a row with net-negative emissions.
evita: Avoids up to {g} Gt a year
captura: Removes up to {g} Gt a year
g_hola: Hi! I'm Ceiba. I'll show you how this works, one bit at a time. The idea is simple: cool the planet down, using solutions that already exist.
g_temp: This matters most: Earth is 1.35 °C warmer than before the Industrial Revolution. Every tenth counts: more heat means more fires, droughts and hurricanes.
g_emis: Why is it warming? Because of the gases we release. Humanity emits about 57 Gt a year. A Gt (gigatonne) is a billion tonnes. As long as this number is above zero, the planet keeps warming.
g_meta: Here's the history: the orange line is temperature, the teal one is emissions. You win when temperature falls 10 years in a row with emissions below zero, meaning you remove more than you release.
g_barras: Cutting CO₂ isn't enough. Look after Life (biodiversity) and Hope (the people pushing for change). If either hits zero, you lose. You also lose if the planet passes 3 °C.
g_tocar: Let's start with a city. The blinking tiles are cities: tap one. I've turned Bogotá towards you.
g_cajon: Each card is a real solution, measured by Project Drawdown, a group of scientists who calculated how much each one can cut the world's emissions. The green number is how much it would avoid if the whole planet adopted it. Pick one and build it.
g_recursos: Building costs energy and materials. They refill every year, but they have a cap: what you don't spend is lost. You don't save money here; you invest in the world.
g_siguiente: Each turn is a year. When you can't afford anything else, end the year and see what happened.
g_despues: Read the card: it tells you how emissions and temperature changed, and what happened around the world.
g_mejorar: Solutions don't change the world overnight: they start slow and speed up as they spread. Tap one of your buildings to upgrade it (up to level 5). And careful: not everything that glitters works. Now the planet is yours.
g_a_trampa: Oops. That solution was a trap: Project Drawdown rates it not recommended. It looked cheap and fast, but its real effect was tiny and it harms Life. You can demolish it: tap the building with the red sign.
g_a_era2: New solutions unlocked: solar farms, offshore wind, ecosystem restoration and more. Restoration doesn't just avoid emissions: it pulls CO₂ out of the air. You'll need it to get below zero.
g_a_evento: A disaster knocked down some buildings. More heat brings more events. Life softens them, and mangroves and salt marshes protect their coasts.
g_a_inflexion: You crossed a tipping point: a change on Earth that doesn't come back, like thawing permafrost. It releases emissions you can't switch off. Better not cross the next ones.
g_a_esperanza: Hope is falling. It rises when people see results (emissions or temperature going down) and with people-centred solutions like public transit or gardens. Spend it wisely: big policies are paid with Hope.
g_a_vida: Life is in danger. Protect and restore ecosystems: forests, peatlands, mangroves. Heat and traps drain it.
g_a_negativas: Emissions below zero! You now remove more than you release. Temperature can finally start to fall.
g_a_racha: Temperature has been falling for a few years. Keep it up for 10 in a row and you reverse climate change.
g_a_recursos: You have spare energy and the cap will waste it. Spend it: upgrading what you have counts too.
tip_temp: Temperature: how much warmer Earth is than before industry (1850-1900). At 3 °C you lose.
tip_emis: Net emissions: the gases the world releases in a year, minus what's removed. 1 Gt = a billion tonnes of CO₂ equivalent. Get them below zero.
tip_ener: Energy: refills every year. Solar, wind and efficiency produce it (every LED bulb frees energy for something else). It has a cap.
tip_mat: Materials: refill every year. Recycling and compost add more. They have a cap.
tip_vida: Life: the planet's biodiversity. More Life means nature removes more CO₂ and disasters hit softer. At 0 you lose.
tip_esp: Hope: the people pushing for change. High Hope makes everything cheaper. It pays for big policies. At 0 you lose.
gl_drawdown_txt: A nonprofit that reviewed hundreds of climate solutions and calculated how much each one can reduce emissions. The game's 166 solutions come from its Drawdown Explorer (2025). Some are rated not recommended: in the game they're traps.
gl_gt_txt: Gigatonnes of CO₂ equivalent per year. A gigatonne is a billion tonnes. "Equivalent" because methane and other gases are counted as the CO₂ that would warm the same. Today the world emits about 57 Gt a year (UNEP, 2024).
gl_temp_txt: Warming above pre-industrial times. It follows all the CO₂ ever accumulated: while we emit, it rises; if we emit below zero, it falls slowly. Methane warms hard but doesn't last, so cutting it cools fast.
gl_netas_txt: When you remove more CO₂ than you release: restoring forests, peatlands, mangroves, or with technology. It's the only way temperature goes down.
gl_adopcion_txt: How much of a solution's potential the world already uses. It grows in an S-curve: slow, then fast, then full. Upgrading a solution pushes it.
gl_trampas_txt: Solutions Project Drawdown doesn't recommend: carbon capture on coal plants, corn ethanol, ocean fertilization... They look cheap and fast. Later it turns out their effect was tiny and they harm Life.
gl_politicas_txt: Big decisions, like closing coal plants, paid with Hope. They cut a whole sector's emissions at once.
gl_inflexion_txt: Parts of Earth that change for good past a certain heat: permafrost, corals, the Amazon (Armstrong McKay et al., 2022).
